'''Emil Schnell''' (born 10 November 1953) is a German physicist and former politician of the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany]] (SPD).

He served as the GDR's last [[Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (East Germany)|minister for post and telecommunications]] in the [[De Maizière cabinet|cabinet]] of [[Lothar de Maizière]].

== Early life and education ==
From 1960 to 1968, Schnell attended the [[Polytechnic Secondary School]], followed by completing his ''[[Abitur]]'' (university entrance qualification) in 1972. From 1972 to 1975, he served in the [[National People's Army]] (NVA).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |year=2009 |title=Schnell, Emil |url=https://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/de/recherche/kataloge-datenbanken/biographische-datenbanken/emil-schnell |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de |series=Wer war wer in der DDR? |publisher=[[Federal Foundation for the Reappraisal of the SED Dictatorship]] |language=de}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |year=2007 |title=Schnell Emil |url=https://webarchiv.bundestag.de/archive/2007/0206/mdb/mdb14/bio/S/schneem0.html |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=webarchiv.bundestag.de |publisher=Internet-Dienst des Deutschen Bundestages |language=de}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Ministerbiografie |url=https://deutsche-einheit-1990.de/ministerien/ministerium-fuer-post-und-meldewesen/ministerbiografie/ |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=Deutsche Einheit 1990 |publisher=[[Federal Foundation for the Reappraisal of the SED Dictatorship]] |language=de}}</ref>

He studied [[physics]] at the [[Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg#History|Technical University of Magdeburg]] from 1975 to 1980, earning a degree as a graduate [[physicist]] ([[Diplom#Germany|Dipl.-Phys.]]).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

Schnell then worked as a [[Research fellow|scientific assistant]] at the same university until 1983. Starting in 1983, he was a research associate at the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin#AdW (1972–1989)|Academy of Sciences of the GDR]] and completed his doctorate ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) in 1984.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

From 1988, he served as a department head at the Academy of Sciences' High-Pressure Research Institute in [[Potsdam]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Pyanoe |first=Steffi |date=2020-03-18 |title=Heute vor 30 Jahren: Erinnerung an die letzte Volkskammer-Wahl in der DDR |url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/potsdam/landeshauptstadt/erinnerung-an-die-letzte-volkskammer-wahl-in-der-ddr-7924504.html |access-date=2024-12-01 |work=Der Tagesspiegel Online |language=de-DE |issn=1865-2263}}</ref>

==Political career==
===de Maizière Government===
During the [[Peaceful Revolution]], in October 1989, Schnell joined the newly reconstituted [[Social Democratic Party in the GDR]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> He became one of the founding members of the SPD in [[Potsdam]],<ref name=":3" /> serving as its managing director during the 1990 election campaign.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

[[1990 East German general election|In the first free elections in the GDR]], Schnell was elected to the [[Volkskammer]] in March 1990 for [[Bezirk Potsdam]], being the ninth-placed candidate on the SPD's list. He was thereafter appointed as [[Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (East Germany)|minister for post and telecommunications]] in the [[De Maizière cabinet|cabinet]] of [[Lothar de Maizière]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

During Schnell's tenure, the ministry focused on modernizing East Germany's postal and telecommunications infrastructure to align with [[West Germany|West German]] standards. This initiative aimed to enhance private communication, support economic growth, and address the GDR's outdated systems, including long postal delivery times and a poorly developed telecommunications network. Significant investments were required, alongside efforts to integrate approximately 130,000 employees from the [[Deutsche Post of the GDR]] into the [[Deutsche Bundespost]]. Schnell additionally raised the postage against the resistance of other SPD ministers.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ministerium für Post- und Fernmeldewesen |url=https://deutsche-einheit-1990.de/ministerien/ministerium-fuer-post-und-meldewesen/ |access-date=2024-12-01 |website=Deutsche Einheit 1990 |publisher=[[Federal Foundation for the Reappraisal of the SED Dictatorship]] |language=de}}</ref>

In August 1990, Schnell and all other SPD ministers resigned in the aftermath of de Maizière's dismissal of SPD finance minister [[Walter Romberg]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> Hans-Jürgen Niehof, one of Schnell's [[Secretary of state#Germany|state secretaries]], served as acting minister until [[German reunification]].

===Reunified Germany===
Schnell was one of 144 [[Volkskammer]] members [[Co-option|co-opted]] to the [[Bundestag]] following [[German reunification]] on 3 October 1990. He remained a [[Member of the German Bundestag|member of the Bundestag]] until the end of the 14th legislative period in October 2002,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> retiring from politics. In the [[1990 German federal election|1990]], [[1994 German federal election|1994]], and [[1998 German federal election|1998 federal elections]], he won the direct mandate in the [[Potsdam – Potsdam-Mittelmark II – Teltow-Fläming II#History|Potsdam constituency]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

Schnell now lives as a freelance physicist in Potsdam.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> He is married and has two children.
